analogs.covers: Almost everything: lazy basker, water's-edge ambush on big land animals, death rolls, males holding a stretch of water

headline: A Nile crocodile with sea legs: lazy basker, ambush at the water's edge, death rolls.

setting.label: Rivers, estuaries, beaches and island crossings
setting.note: Tolerates brackish and salt water, so it is often found near estuaries and beaches and swims the open ocean between islands. Basks on banks by day and returns to deep water at night.

playsLike: You are an Apex semi-aquatic ambusher with 6,000 combat weight. Every hunt starts in the water; you may chase onto land only until your stamina runs out (sprint 550 for 40 s) unless you have already fractured the prey. You hunt alone, may take any tier, may third-party any fight within 2 body lengths of your water, and death-roll prey in the water. Males hold a stretch of water against other males and Sarcosuchus, while females wander between territories.

why.text: Lies beneath the surface by the shore waiting for land animals to come too close, the Nile crocodile's river-crossing ambush (official inspiration).
Basks for long periods with jaws open to cool the brain, and slips back underwater when prey appears.
Opens its jaws for scavengers to pick its teeth clean and tolerates them at its kills.
Males defend a stretch of water from other males and keep an uneasy truce with neighbours; females may pass through.
Clamps prey in the water and rolls violently to tear it apart.

notLike: Nile crocodiles are mostly freshwater animals; Deinosuchus also lives on beaches and crosses the open sea like a saltwater crocodile.
twist: Give the Nile crocodile a saltwater crocodile's sea legs and you have Deinosuchus.
